Subject: Proposal and perf/memory matrix for Aurora reserved commit

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, attached is a compact proposal that maps committed throughput to GPU pool composition (A100 80GB, H100 80GB, L40S 48GB) and the expected 95th/99th p99 latency envelope for your typical token mix. Highlights:

- Two commit tiers: 200k token/s sustained (Tier A) and 500k token/s sustained (Tier B) with burst lanes.
- Perf/$ shows H100 winning for large-context, low-batch workloads; A100 is better for long-lived KV-cache workloads where memory matters; L40S offers the best perf/$ for dense batching (inference-heavy, short context) but has smaller memory.
- Included a column for recommended memory (40/80/96GB per GPU), expected throughput per GPU, and projected monthly committed spend.

Attachments: aurora-dedicated-proposal-v3.xlsx (pricing matrix), perf-simulations-a100-h100-l40s.csv (simulation inputs).

Quick ask: can you confirm target 95th latency SLO (we assumed <=120ms for chat baseline) and whether you prioritize token-dollar or tail latency? That changes optimal mix.

I'll loop in Neha who ran the perf sims.

Thanks,
Mina

Hi Sam —

Short answers while Neha pulls numbers for your exact mix:
- Burst lanes: reserved pool can be configured with a 20% short-term burst buffer (60 minutes) that sits above sustained throughput and is billed as part of the commit but throttled in extreme cases. For longer bursts we recommend a small pay-as-you-go overflow with pre-authorized fallback.
- For mixed workloads we usually propose a split pool: 60% H100s (chat, long-context) + 40% L40S (dense batched embed/rerank) as a starting point for Tier B. That gives predictable latency for chat and cost efficiency for embeddings.

We can do term-based concessions: 12-month commit gives X% off list, 24-month gives more — details in the attached pricing sheet. If you can do a firm 24-month commit to the Tier B baseline, we can offer an additional performance credit that effectively reduces per-token price when average utilization >70%.

Will follow up with detailed perf sims.

-Vivek
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Proposal and perf/memory matrix for Aurora reserved commit

Sam/Mina/Vivek —

I've attached a lean CSV with the simulation inputs (perf-simulations-a100-h100-l40s.csv) and a short summary here:

- Long-context (8k tokens): H100@80GB gives ~1.8x throughput per GPU vs A100@80GB for the same batch=1 latency profile; p95 latency improves by ~30ms on average. Memory headroom on H100 helps with KV-cache residency for pinned sessions.
- Embeds/rerank (64 tokens, batch 64): L40S shows ~1.4x perf/$ compared to H100 because of higher batching efficiency and lower instance cost; memory is sufficient for short contexts.
- Hybrid utilization model (expected split 55% chat / 45% embeds): the blended perf/$ for a 60/40 H100/L40S mix is ~12% better than all-H100 for the same tail latency target.

Caveats: if you need the absolute lowest p99 for chat (e.g., <100ms), all-H100 with higher overprovisioning might be required and that shifts cost materially.

I've also added a sheet with a sample commit schedule and a utilization credit clause (see column F in the XLSX). Happy to hop on a quick call to run through the numbers live.

-Neha
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
